title: Tortilla Chips 300g

drivers.name: Price increase (3.7%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks at $3.97 saw sales at 85% and 61% of baseline; noise-adjusted average x0.73; this price is new to this product, so shrink toward 1.0—effect set to -15%

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: No direct closure data, but 10% demand loss plausible for a full day of lost sales; store-level closure data not available, so conservative estimate

drivers.name: Thanksgiving (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect is x1.0; past two occurrences show no consistent lift (x1.21, x0.86); no evidence of significant driver

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 124.1. Thanksgiving (Thu) has a weak historical lift (x1.03, noise-adjusted x1.0), so no meaningful uplift. Price increased 3.7% to $3.97—past 3.97 price weeks (2026-09-28, 10-05) saw sales drop to 106 and 75 (x0.85, x0.61 vs baseline). The store closure on Monday (Thanksgiving week) likely suppresses early sales; no prior closure data, but similar events reduce demand. No promotion, so no uplift. The classical model’s 1.00 is too high—price increase and closure likely suppress demand. Adjust down with moderate confidence.

  shelf price: 3.97 (+3.7% vs regular price 3.83)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 124.1 | 5%-95%: 77.3 - 200.5 | 10%-90%: 88.8 - 170.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-29% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
